paper_metadata.title: High-temperature creep behavior of gamma Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb alloy additively manufactured by electron beam melting

According to Weertman et al. [43], the creep mechanism is dominated by grain-boundary sliding at n =2, by dislocation glide at n = 3, and by dislocation climb at n = 5. When evaluating the creep mechanism of the two samples according to the estimated stress exponent (n), it was assumed that the creep deformation was dominated by dislocation glide and dislocation climb in the case of the EBM-built sample.

After the 750 °C high-temperature creep test, the EBM-built sample with the NG structure had lower creep resistance. This is attributed to the reduction of the dislocation barrier (e.g., γ/α2 interface) and the YSA in lamellar α2 being more prominent than that in γ.
